item.description:

Join Ty the Fungi, a seasoned local forager with nearly 15 years of experience, and learn how to find, identify, and responsibly harvest wild mushrooms—from prized edibles to those best left untouched. Discover the principles of ethical foraging and deepen your connection to the landscape through this immersive, hands-on exploration.
Meet at The Lodge’s Fireside Lounge, and we’ll caravan together to the foraging site.

Join experienced yoga and meditation instructor MaryEllen Whitton for a 90-minute experience combining gentle movement, breathwork, meditation, and Yoga Nidra—a guided practice designed to promote profound relaxation, calm the nervous system, and restore a sense of balance.
You'll be guided into a state of deep rest, allowing your body to relax while your mind remains gently aware. No previous yoga experience is necessary. Simply come as you are and give yourself the gift of stillness.

item.title: Lecture Two | The Social Sculpture: How Art Can Shape Society — Tue Nov 17, 7:30 PM — Laguna Lab
item.description:
As part of the 2-week art exhibition, STIMULANT, Apocalypse Studio presents the 2nd lecture in their 2-part series.
The studio’s founder spent many years working with leaders in twenty countries on some of humanity’s toughest social challenges, from war and poverty to the destruction of nature, drug abuse, immigration, and violence. He will share his insights from these years, focusing on why only the domain of culture can rebalance systemic breakdown and social decay. He will introduce what he calls the "8th great art", Social Sculpture, to add to the 7 already known (Painting, Sculpture, Literature, Architecture, Theater, Film, and Music). Social Sculpture is the art form of artfully co-creating society actively and together.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat, Sebastopol Calendar

item.title: Art Salon | The Future of Culture: the Role and Purpose of Art — Fri Nov 20, 5:00 PM — Laguna Lab
item.description:
In 18th- and 19th-century Paris, salons brought artists, writers and serious minds together to talk about art, ideas and the questions of their day. Many new ideas were first tried out in those rooms, in conversation, long before they reached the wider world.
Our salon borrows from that spirit. Surrounded by the works of the STIMULANT art exhibition, we'll gather to ask what role art and culture can play in a society in crisis, and how we might respond - individually and together - to it.
Join us for an evening of art, mingling, a light dinner, and facilitated dialogue with questions and provocations to stimulate new ways of seeing how we might nourish culture for social change.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Sebastopol Calendar

Lavender Workshop: Create, Relax & Enjoy
Spend a relaxing afternoon immersed in the soothing scent of lavender! In this hands-on workshop, you'll create your own lavender products to enjoy at home or share as thoughtful gifts.
Each participant will make and take home two lavender sprays and two lavender sugar scrubs. All materials are provided, so just bring your creativity and get ready for a fun, fragrant afternoon! Additional sprays and scrubs will also be available for purchase.
Additional sprays and scrubs will also be available for purchase.
All materials included.

MaryEllen Whitton is an award-winning author, speaker, personal growth coach, and workshop facilitator guiding others to create what comes next with greater clarity, confidence, and intention.

item.title: California Redwood Chorale 20th Anniversary concerts — Sun Nov 22, 3:00 PM — Jacuzzi Family Vineyards
item.description:
The California Redwood Chorale is returning to the Jacuzzi Barrel Room to sing for you as we celebrate our 20th Anniversary.
This group of skilled singers is known for singing across the choices of choral music, from "Bohemian Rhapsody" to Mozart! This season we will honor Dolly Parton by singing her tender "Light of a Clear Blue Morning" as well as "Dirait-on" by Morten Lauridsen, "Chorale: Hymn" by Karl Jenkins, "I'll be Seeing You" by Habermann and Fain, "Ad Astra" by Narverud, "Time after Time" by Cyndi Lauper, "O Love" by Elaine Hagenberg, "The Awakening" by Martin and more!
We are so thrilled to be returning to the Barrel Room. Won't you please join us? SingChronous will be guest artists at the Jacuzzi concert.
$30 at the door cash or check to CRC

item.title: Annual Free Thanksgiving Dinner — Thu Nov 26, 3:00 PM — Sonoma Veterans Memorial Hall
item.description:
Thursday, November 26, 2026
Held annually at the Sonoma Veterans Memorial Hall at 126 First Street West. Doors open at 3:00 PM and meals will be provided until the food runs out.
Meals will be available on a first come, first served basis and all are welcome to attend. There is no cost to attend, however, donations are gratefully accepted to help offset the cost of producing the event.
For years, the Sonoma Community Center, Sonoma’s Rotary, Vintage House and many, many others have teamed up to serve over 500 free Thanksgiving dinners to local residents. Led by an all-volunteer crew, the free dinner has become a much-loved tradition in the Sonoma Valley, bringing together a broad cross-section of the community. As always, the meal is made using locally sourced, fresh ingredients and includes all the traditional Thanksgiving fare. item.title: Mushroom Foraging — Sun Nov 29, 9:00 AM — The Sea Ranch Lodge
item.description:
Wild mushroom season has arrived on the Sonoma Coast, where misty forests and coastal meadows nurture a dazzling diversity of fungi for curious foragers and culinary enthusiasts alike.
Join Ty the Fungi, a seasoned local forager with nearly 15 years of experience, and learn how to find, identify, and responsibly harvest wild mushrooms—from prized edibles to those best left untouched. Discover the principles of ethical foraging and deepen your connection to the landscape through this immersive, hands-on exploration.
Meet at The Lodge’s Fireside Lounge, and we’ll caravan together to the foraging site.
$160 per person, $100 (ages 10-16). Space is limited. This adventure is recommended for participants with moderate to advanced hiking experience.
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: Soul Motion®: Body Prayer every Sunday in person — Sun Nov 29, 10:00 AM — Wischemann Hall
item.description: BODY PRAYER IS A FACILITATED EVENT DEVOTED TO INQUIRY INTO EMBODIED CONSCIOUSNESS THROUGH MOVEMENT. This class is offered every Sunday morning, and led by Zuza Engler or another teacher. It is usually attended by a vibrant & diverse bunch of welcoming and friendly people, some of whom have practiced Soul Motion® for years, while some ~ never before. What to expect Guidance and structure are part of every week’s class as we travel across the four landscapes of Soul Motion®: Dance Infinite (prayer space) Dance Community (ensemble) Dance Communion (duet) Dance Intimate (solo) Practices, structures, and points of view are offered to facilitate the journey. Participants are invited to travel across all landscapes, not just their favorite one: dancing by oneself, in duet, in ensemble with several people and eventually the whole room, or witnessing in stillness the beauty of another’s or of everyone’s dance.
